Command: Be Reconciled to Your Brother First
Summary: Jesus' priority command: before bringing your gift to the altar, first go and be reconciled to a brother who has something against you.
Commandment: If your brother has anything against you, leave your gift, first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.
Application: Worship is not a cover for an unmended breach. The command is urgent — agree with your adversary quickly — because unresolved wrong hardens into judgment.
Purpose: Scripture's own reason in context: lest the adversary deliver you to the judge (Matthew 5:25).
Function: Worship waits on reconciliation — that is the order Jesus sets here. This comes from the New Testament, not from Sinai, so the old threefold division does not apply to it. Its goal was to keep worship from becoming a cover for an unmended breach: leave the gift, go and be reconciled first. The evil it addressed was unresolved wrong left to harden into judgment. It restrained that evil with urgency: agree with your adversary quickly, before the breach becomes a case before the judge.
